title: Hi everyone - Greetings from the UK

posts.topic_title: Hi everyone - Greetings from the UK
posts.author: Jem
posts.post_subject: Hi everyone - Greetings from the UK
posts.content_md:
Hi everyone

My name is Jem (short for Jeremy!). I live in the north of england, West Yorkshire to be more precise. I'm 48 yrs young and I work in Ophthalmic Optics.

I've had an unhealthy interest in Lasers for quite a while now but have never really progressed beyond the 'Wow, isn't it amazing how far that little red dot will shine", i've also fiddled about with lenses and lasers but nothing too technical 

Just recently though I had a few spare minutes and spent them scaning through stuff for sale on Ebay. I placed a bid for a new JDS Uniphase HeNe 632.8nm Mod1125p laser, don't ask me why I wanted, or should I say 'needed' this(my wife says too much Southern Comfort). Anyway I won the auction and so this is the first 'proper' laser that i've owned.

When it arrived I started to wonder 'why?' had I bought this, after a while I decided it must have been divine intervention Perhaps someone up there just wants me to get hooked on yet another hobby! (it'll have to fit somewhere in between playing the digeridoo, target shooting, fiddling with computers and programming (currently trying to upgrade my mind from VB6 to .net)!

So, here I am - Hooked on lasers, working in optics and thinking about having a go at Holography. 

So, now a question... Will the laser I just bought be suitable for a starter in holography or will I have to start looking for another to add to the collection?

Oh, here's another... How many holography 'addicts' are there in the UK, is there anyone near or just south of Leeds?

Cheers

Jem

posts.topic_title: Hi everyone - Greetings from the UK
posts.author: John Klayer
posts.post_subject: Hi everyone - Greetings from the UK
posts.content_md:
Welcome Jem!

Yes, the 1125P should work well for holography. It is 5 mW and polarized. Warning! Holography can become an addiction! Just hop on a plane and come to the PCGIII on 20 May at my home in the South of the USA and meet some holographers.

posts.post_subject: Hi everyone - Greetings from the UK
posts.content_md:
Hi John

Thanks for the reply, the 1125p Laser I have states that it is 10mw on the label. However, I note that on the pdf spec sheet it is recorded as being 5mw. Is the label simply stating a peak output power?

Shame about the PCG111 in May, I won't have a chance of getting there as I'll be in Phoenix at the end of April for the Kodak lens conference (not a conference at all really, just an excuse for a few optically minded Brits to chill out for a while around the pool and see the Grand Canyon etc.)

Cheers

Jem

Welcome! Really a laser, film, processing and a lens are all that is required to get your feet wet.

Take a look at the HoloWiki for some tips:
